content.rendered:
Every name of God this week has described what He does. This final one describes who you are to Him: not a servant crying out to a Master, but a child crying out to Abba.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, August 20, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“For you did not receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption by whom we cry out, ‘Abba, Father.’”
Romans 8:15 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Ten days ago, this series began with Elohim, the God who creates from nothing. It closes today with a name that is not really a title at all — it is the cry of a child. Abba was the intimate Aramaic word a Jewish child used for their father, close to what “Dad” or “Papa” carries in English: affectionate, familiar, nothing like the formal distance of a subject addressing a sovereign.

Every name we have studied this week — Provider, Healer, Banner, Peace, Shepherd, Righteousness, Almighty, the God who is present — describes something God does for His people. Abba describes something different: who you have become to Him. Paul is explicit about the contrast in Romans 8:15 — the alternative to the Spirit of adoption is “the spirit of bondage again to fear,” the posture of a slave who serves out of fear of a Master. But those who belong to Christ have received something else entirely: adoption, with all its legal and relational weight, and permission to cry out with the same word Jesus Himself used in Gethsemane: “Abba, Father, all things are possible for You” (Mark 14:36).

The Amplified Bible draws out the depth of the cry: “you have received [the] Spirit of adoption as sons [the Spirit producing sonship] by which we [joyfully] cry, ‘Abba! Father!’” (Romans 8:15 AMP). Joyfully — not tentatively, not as a stranger unsure of their welcome, but as a child who knows exactly whose house they are standing in.

This is where every name of God this series has been leading. Elohim’s power, Jehovah Jireh’s provision, Jehovah Rapha’s healing, Jehovah Nissi’s banner, Jehovah Shalom’s peace, Jehovah Raah’s shepherding, Jehovah Tsidkenu’s righteousness, El Shaddai’s sufficiency, Jehovah Shammah’s presence — none of it is the transaction of a distant deity dispensing favours to servants who perform well enough. It is the ordinary provision of a Father for children He has adopted permanently, at great cost, and calls His own. Paul finishes the thought two verses later: “and if children, then heirs — heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ” (Romans 8:17).

Whatever name of God met you somewhere in this series — whatever provision, healing, peace, or presence you needed this week — receive it today not as a transaction from a distant deity but as the ordinary care of a Father who has already called you His own. Cry out. Abba is listening.

Prayer

Father, thank You that I am not a servant crying out to a Master I must impress, but a child crying out to a Father who has already adopted me. Every name I have studied this week — Provider, Healer, Shepherd, Peace — is not a transaction. It is the care of a Father for His child. I cry out to You today: Abba, Father. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My God is Abba, Father. I am not a slave to fear but a child of adoption. I cry out to Him joyfully, not tentatively. I am an heir of God and a joint heir with Christ, and every name of God I have studied this week belongs to me as my Father’s provision.

  • Galatians 4:6-7 (NKJV): No longer a slave but a son
  • Mark 14:36 (NKJV): Jesus’ own cry of Abba, Father
